acceptance_tests: The same preset, seed, control history, and render duration produce byte-identical DrumHit and allocator traces across supported outer block sizes.
At enthusiasm zero, repeated phrases contain the same normalized authored events; increasing a lane complexity never removes one of that lane's base-layer events.
Rational timing fixtures place ordinary, triplet, quintuplet, and odd-meter events at deterministic integer sample offsets without a fixed sixteen-step representation.
Four pooled Braids cores render the six logical lanes through the specified deterministic choke, idle, tail, steal, and drop ordering, including same-sample overload fixtures.
The frozen stereo 48 kHz renders contain no integer overflow or hard clipping, remain within the declared peak and DC bounds, and match across supported outer block sizes.
The authoritative Mutable source-release references, exact shared 12-file Braids and 5-file stmlib physical closures, and reusable non-provider adapter validate before the instrument configures.

The exact Tide Pit regular Launch Control 3 topology fingerprint is reused, all 16 encoder and eight button selectors are generated, and every MIDI value, wrong-channel, unknown, inactive-mode, press, release, and invalid-value case is exhaustively checked.
Accepted LC3 mappings update only the public Controls or one-shot fill semantic; raw MIDI bytes never enter the rhythm generator, DrumHit stream, allocator, or synthesis pool.

The pure UI projection and streaming-control snapshot have focused tests; on-screen controls and MIDI controller messages traverse the same generated LC3 mapping and UI feedback reflects accepted public state.

The audio callback advances a persistent fixed-capacity rational-time scheduler and four-voice Braids pool without locks, allocation, file I/O, JSON, or UI work; accepted continuous controls affect the next callback block, with shape targets slewed over exactly 128 samples.

Complexity and enthusiasm changes affect only future un-crossed events, tempo preserves musical phase, swing affects only future eligible off-eighth events, rhythm selection restarts the selected study at its downbeat at the next block while preserving synthesis tails, and Fill starts one normalized one-bar overlay at the next block.

The optional standalone JUCE application target builds and links from an operator-supplied tree whose complete fingerprint matches the accepted JUCE source-release extraction manifest, with network fetching disabled.
The frozen offline render manifest remains byte-identical after the UI/host addition.

Fifteen independently authored rhythm-study descriptors span 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, 9/8, and 10/8, validate meter-local rational bounds, and produce deterministic cycle lengths, event traces, coherent variations, and fills without claiming cultural authenticity.

Buttons CC40-45 select or toggle exactly one corresponding logical lane, CC46 dispatches Fill, CC47 advances the fifteen-item rhythm bank once per press, and bottom encoders CC28-33 mutate only the selected lane's six bounded voice-shape values.

A neutral six-parameter shape bank is audio-equivalent to the authored lane recipes; non-neutral Tune, Timbre, Color, Decay, Pitch Env/Punch, and Level resolve within declared bounds, update sounding matching-lane voices plus future hits, and do not change DrumHit timing or provenance.

The fixed-capacity streaming engine produces byte-identical semantic hit and allocation traces and signed PCM for an identical control timeline across supported outer block partitions, and a synthetic callback-kernel benchmark reports measurements without promoting them to live real-time or device evidence.
Instrument Lab index, topology, authority hashes, promotion-needs, and implementation handoff validations pass without claiming accepted-runtime, target, device, listening, or production evidence.

Expand the proof bank to fifteen independently authored rhythm studies and bind the regular LC3 bottom six buttons and encoders to direct selected-lane shaping under the frozen revision 0.6 laws.

A rational-time bank of fifteen independently authored rhythm studies and generated C++ descriptors whose freshness, attribution metadata, and meter bounds are checked exhaustively.
A portable C++17 rhythm generator, semantic DrumHit stream, fixed-capacity streaming scheduler, four-voice allocator, Braids wrapper, fixed-point envelopes, decimator, and offline renderer.
A generated regular Launch Control 3 descriptor set plus a pure channel/CC/value-to-public-control adapter with exhaustive mapping and application tests.
A pure accepted-state UI projection and lock-free atomic control-snapshot boundary with focused tests.

An optional JUCE 8.0.15 standalone audition app with six lane cards, fifteen-way rhythm selection, selected-lane six-parameter voice shaping, global performance controls, fill, activity/cycle/callback feedback, streaming stereo playback, and MIDI input selection/diagnostics.

goal.primary_claim: A six-lane authored rational-time rhythm engine can select among independently authored meters and apply persistent per-lane voice shaping while deterministically driving four dynamically reassigned Braids voices without making MIDI, edit focus, or a fixed sixteen-step grid authoritative.
goal.why: The advancement must preserve the proven complexity/event/allocator seams while testing meter-dependent phrase timing and reusable logical-lane synthesis recipes through the remaining LC3 surface.

in: Fifteen independently authored six-lane rhythm studies spanning at least five meters, including situated samba-family, maracatu, candombe, chacarera, aksak, and jhaptal studies, with reduced rational positions, 16-bit monotone base thresholds, explicit variation groups, meter-local fills, source relationships, and no authenticity claim.

Semantic absolute-frame DrumHit events with lane, U15 velocity, U8 articulation, source ordinal, and stable same-frame ordering.
Four fully pooled Braids cores, full-storage reset on reassignment, per-hit fixed-point amplitude and parameter envelopes, deterministic choking, stealing, dropping, tail bridge, gain, and pan.

The Tide Pit regular Launch Control 3 Custom Mode topology and an instrument-owned pure mapping: CC20-25 lane complexities, CC26 enthusiasm, CC27 tempo, CC28-33 selected-lane Tune/Timbre/Color/Decay/Pitch Env/Level, CC34 swing, CC35 direct rhythm select, CC40-45 corresponding lane selection/toggle, CC46 Fill, and CC47 rhythm advance.
One persistent six-U7 VoiceShape record per logical lane. Neutral values resolve to authored recipes; editable fields are Tune, Timbre, Color, Decay, Pitch Env/Punch, and Level only.
Core-only Instrument Lab integration and deterministic offline 48 kHz stereo host-signal evidence.

Selectable host MIDI input and receive diagnostics in the optional app, with every accepted message terminating at the generated LC3-to-public-control/state reducer.
A fifteen-item rhythm selector, six numbered lane-shaping buttons, and a disabled-when-unselected six-knob shaping panel whose feedback is projected from accepted state.
